sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'pi mahātejās tac chṛṅgaṃ saptabhiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghāna sutīkṣṇāgrais tad vikīrṇaṃ papāta ha
english: Rāvaṇa of great blazing energy then struck that peak with seven arrows tipped with keen points, and shattered it fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tad vikīrṇaṃ gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā haricamūpatiḥ kālāgnir iva jajvāla krodhena paravīrahā
english: Seeing that mountain-peak shattered, the commander of the monkey host — that slayer of enemy heroes — blazed up with fury like the fire of universal dissolution.

sanskrit: so 'śvakarṇān dhavān sālāṃś cūtāṃś cāpi supuṣpitān anyāṃś ca vividhān vṛkṣān nīlaś cikṣepa saṃyuge
english: Then Nīla hurled in battle aśvakarṇa trees, dhava trees, śāla trees, and well-blossoming mango trees, as well as many other diverse trees.

sanskrit: sa tān vṛkṣān samāsādya praticiccheda rāvaṇaḥ abhyavarṣat sughoreṇa śaravarṣeṇa pāvakim
english: Rāvaṇa met those trees and cut them apart, then pelted the son of Agni with a most terrible shower of arrows.

sanskrit: abhivṛṣṭaḥ śaraugheṇa megheneva mahācalaḥ hrasvaṃ kṛtvā tadā rūpaṃ dhvajāgre nipapāta ha
english: Pelted by that torrent of arrows as a great mountain is by a storm-cloud, he contracted his form to a tiny size and alighted on the tip of Rāvaṇa's flagstaff.

sanskrit: pāvakātmajam ālokya dhvajāgre samavasthitam jajvāla rāvaṇaḥ krodhāt tato nīlo nanāda ha
english: Seeing the son of Agni perched upon the top of his flagstaff, Rāvaṇa blazed with anger — and then Nīla let out a roar.

sanskrit: dhvajāgre dhanuṣaś cāgre kirīṭāgre ca taṃ harim lakṣmaṇo 'tha hanūmāṃś ca dṛṣṭvā rāmaś ca vismitāḥ
english: Seeing that monkey leap from flagstaff-tip to bow-tip to crown-tip, Lakṣmaṇa, Hanūmān, and Rāma were all filled with wonder.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'pi mahātejāḥ kapilāghavavismitaḥ astram āhārayām āsa dīptam āgneyam adbhutam
english: Rāvaṇa of great blazing energy, astonished at the monkey's agility, then invoked the flaming and wondrous Āgneya weapon.

sanskrit: tatas te cukruśur hṛṣṭā labdhalakṣyāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ nīlalāghavasaṃbhrāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇam āhave
english: Then the monkeys, having achieved their aim, shouted with joy, seeing Rāvaṇa thrown into confusion in battle by Nīla's nimbleness.

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ ca nādena saṃrabdho rāvaṇas tadā saṃbhramāviṣṭahṛdayo na kiṃ cit pratyapadyata
english: Enraged by the clamour of the monkeys, Rāvaṇa at that moment was seized with confusion of heart and could not recover his composure.

sanskrit: āgneyenātha saṃyuktaṃ gṛhītvā rāvaṇaḥ śaram dhvajaśīrṣasthitaṃ nīlam udaikṣata niśācaraḥ
english: Then the night-ranger Rāvaṇa took up an arrow charged with the Āgneya weapon and looked up at Nīla, who stood upon the top of the flagstaff.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ kape lāghavayukto 'si māyayā parayānayā
english: Then Rāvaṇa, the great-blazing lord of rākṣasas, spoke: "You are possessed of agility, O monkey, by some supreme magical power.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ khalu rakṣasva yadi śaknoṣi vānara tāni tāny ātmarūpāṇi sṛjase tvam anekaśaḥ
english: Protect your life if you can, O monkey — you multiply those forms of yours time and again.

sanskrit: tathāpi tvāṃ mayā muktaḥ sāyako 'straprayojitaḥ jīvitaṃ parirakṣantaṃ jīvitād bhraṃśayiṣyati
english: Even so, the arrow discharged by me and empowered by this weapon shall dislodge you from your life, however much you strive to preserve it."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhū rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ saṃdhāya bāṇam astreṇa camūpatim atāḍayat
english: Having spoken thus, mighty-armed Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, fitted the arrow with the weapon and struck the commander of the host.

sanskrit: so 'strayuktena bāṇena nīlo vakṣasi tāḍitaḥ nirdahyamānaṃ sahasā nipapāta mahītale
english: Nīla, struck in the chest by that arrow empowered with the weapon, burned as it were and suddenly fell to the ground.

sanskrit: pitṛmāhātmyasaṃyogād ātmanaś cāpi tejasā jānubhyām apatad bhūmau na ca prāṇair vyayujyata
english: Through the greatness of his father's glory and his own inherent energy, he fell only to his knees on the earth and was not parted from his life.

sanskrit: visaṃjñaṃ vānaraṃ dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvo raṇotsukaḥ rathenāmbudanādena saumitrim abhidudruve
english: Seeing the monkey lying senseless, ten-necked Rāvaṇa, eager for battle, charged toward Saumitri in his chariot that roared like a thundercloud.

sanskrit: tam āha saumitrir adīnasattvo visphārayantaṃ dhanur aprameyam anvehi mām eva niśācarendra na vānarāṃs tvaṃ prati yoddhum arhasi
english: Saumitri, of undaunted spirit, spoke to him as he drew his immeasurable bow: "Come against me alone, O lord of the night-rangers — you should not fight against the monkeys."

sanskrit: sa tasya vākyaṃ paripūrṇaghoṣaṃ jyāśabdam ugraṃ ca niśamya rājā āsādya saumitrim avasthitaṃ taṃ kopānvitaṃ vākyam uvāca rakṣaḥ
english: Hearing his words, resonant and full-toned, and the fierce twang of his bowstring, the king approached Saumitri where he stood, and the rākṣasa spoke in anger.

sanskrit: diṣṭyāsi me rāghava dṛṣṭimārgaṃ prāpto 'ntagāmī viparītabuddhiḥ asmin kṣaṇe yāsyasi mṛtyudeśaṃ saṃsādyamāno mama bāṇajālaiḥ
english: "Fortunate for me that you have come within my sight, O Rāghava — you who are perverse of judgment and rushing toward your end. In this very instant you shall journey to the realm of death, battered by my net of arrows."

sanskrit: tam āha saumitrir avismayāno garjantam udvṛttasitāgradaṃṣṭram rājan na garjanti mahāprabhāvā vikatthase pāpakṛtāṃ variṣṭha
english: Saumitri, unperturbed, spoke to him as he roared with upturned white fangs: "The truly mighty do not bellow, O king. You boast too much, O foremost among evil-doers."

sanskrit: jānāmi vīryaṃ tava rākṣasendra balaṃ pratāpaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca avasthito 'haṃ śaracāpapāṇir āgaccha kiṃ moghavikatthanena
english: "I know your valour, O lord of rākṣasas — your strength, your power, and your prowess. I stand here, bow and arrows in hand. Come! What purpose is served by empty boasting?"

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ kupitaḥ sasarja rakṣo'dhipaḥ saptaśarān supuṅkhān tāṃl lakṣmaṇaḥ kāñcanacitrapuṅkhaiś ciccheda bāṇair niśitāgradhāraiḥ
english: Provoked by these words, the angry lord of rākṣasas discharged seven well-feathered arrows; Lakṣmaṇa cut them apart with sharp-edged arrows adorned with golden plumage.

sanskrit: tān prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasā nikṛttān nikṛttabhogān iva pannagendrān laṅkeśvaraḥ krodhavaśaṃ jagāma sasarja cānyān niśitān pṛṣatkān
english: Seeing them suddenly cut down like great serpents with severed coils, the lord of Laṅkā fell under the sway of fury and launched other sharp-pointed arrows.

sanskrit: sa bāṇavarṣaṃ tu vavarṣa tīvraṃ rāmānujaḥ kārmukasaṃprayuktam kṣurārdhacandrottamakarṇibhallaiḥ śarāṃś ca ciccheda na cukṣubhe ca
english: Rāma's younger brother unleashed a fierce rain of arrows from his bow, cutting apart those shafts with razor-headed, crescent-headed, karna, and broad-headed arrows, and remained undisturbed.

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇaś cāśu śarāñ śitāgrān mahendravajrāśanitulyavegān saṃdhāya cāpe jvalanaprakāśān sasarja rakṣo'dhipater vadhāya
english: And Lakṣmaṇa swiftly fitted to his bow sharp-tipped arrows blazing like fire, equal in speed to the thunderbolt of great Indra, and discharged them to slay the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa tān praciccheda hi rākṣasendraś chittvā ca tāṃl lakṣmaṇam ājaghāna śareṇa kālāgnisamaprabheṇa svayambhudattena lalāṭadeśe
english: The lord of rākṣasas cut those arrows apart, and having cut them, struck Lakṣmaṇa in the forehead with an arrow blazing like the fire of final destruction — an arrow given by Svayambhū himself.

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇasāyakārtaś cacāla cāpaṃ śithilaṃ pragṛhya punaś ca saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya kṛcchrāc ciccheda cāpaṃ tridaśendraśatroḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa, wounded by Rāvaṇa's arrow, reeled and grasped his bow feebly; then recovering his senses with difficulty, he cut apart the bow of the enemy of the lord of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: nikṛttacāpaṃ tribhir ājaghāna bāṇais tadā dāśarathiḥ śitāgraiḥ sa sāyakārto vicacāla rājā kṛcchrāc ca saṃjñāṃ punar āsasāda
english: Then the son of Daśaratha struck him — now bereft of his bow — with three sharp-pointed arrows. The king, tortured by those shafts, staggered and only with difficulty regained his senses.

sanskrit: sa kṛttacāpaḥ śaratāḍitaś ca svedārdragātro rudhirāvasiktaḥ jagrāha śaktiṃ samudagraśaktiṃ svayambhudattāṃ yudhi devaśatruḥ
english: His bow severed and his body struck by arrows, his limbs damp with sweat and drenched in blood, the enemy of the gods — of supreme power — seized in battle the śakti given by Svayambhū.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ vidhūmānalasaṃnikāśāṃ vitrāsanīṃ vānaravāhinīnām cikṣepa śaktiṃ tarasā jvalantīṃ saumitraye rākṣasarāṣṭranāthaḥ
english: The lord of the rākṣasa realm swiftly hurled that blazing śakti — like smokeless fire and terrifying to the monkey host — at Saumitri.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ bharatānujo 'strair jaghāna bāṇaiś ca hutāgnikalpaiḥ tathāpi sā tasya viveśa śaktir bhujāntaraṃ dāśarather viśālam
english: The younger brother of Bharata struck that oncoming weapon with missile-charged arrows equal to consecrated fire; yet even so that śakti entered the broad chest of the son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: śaktyā brāmyā tu saumitris tāḍitas tu stanāntare viṣṇor acintyaṃ svaṃ bhāgam ātmānaṃ pratyanusmarat
english: Struck in the chest by that bewildering śakti, Saumitri contemplated within himself his own inconceivable nature as a portion of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tato dānavadarpaghnaṃ saumitriṃ devakaṇṭakaḥ taṃ pīḍayitvā bāhubhyām aprabhur laṅghane 'bhavat
english: Then the thorn of the gods tried to seize Saumitri — destroyer of the pride of dānavas — in his arms, but found himself powerless to lift him.

sanskrit: himavān mandaro merus trailokyaṃ vā sahāmaraiḥ śakyaṃ bhujābhyām uddhartuṃ na saṃkhye bharatānujaḥ
english: Himavān, Mandara, Meru, or even the three worlds together with the immortals might be lifted by his arms in battle — but not the younger brother of Bharata.

sanskrit: athainaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ bhāgaṃ mānuṣaṃ deham āsthitam visaṃjñaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo vismito 'bhavat
english: Then, seeing Lakṣmaṇa — that portion of Viṣṇu dwelling in a human body — lying senseless, Rāvaṇa was filled with astonishment.

sanskrit: atha vāyusutaḥ kruddho rāvaṇaṃ samabhidravat ājaghānorasi kruddho vajrakalpena muṣṭinā
english: Then the son of Vāyu, filled with fury, charged at Rāvaṇa and struck him in the chest with a clenched fist like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tena muṣṭiprahāreṇa rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ jānubhyām apatad bhūmau cacāla ca papāta ca
english: By that blow of the fist, Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, fell to the ground on his knees — he tottered and he fell.

sanskrit: visaṃjñaṃ rāvaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā samare bhīmavikramam ṛṣayo vānarāś caiva nedur devāḥ savāsavāḥ
english: Seeing Rāvaṇa of terrible prowess lying senseless in battle, the sages, the monkeys, and the gods together with Vāsava all shouted with joy.

sanskrit: hanūmān api tejasvī lakṣmaṇaṃ rāvaṇārditam anayad rāghavābhyāśaṃ bāhubhyāṃ parigṛhya tam
english: And Hanūmān, full of energy, took up Lakṣmaṇa — who had been tormented by Rāvaṇa — in his arms and carried him to Rāghava's side.

sanskrit: vāyusūnoḥ suhṛttvena bhaktyā paramayā ca saḥ śatrūṇām aprakampyo 'pi laghutvam agamat kapeḥ
english: By the friendship of the son of Vāyu and his supreme devotion, he who was utterly unshakeable by enemies became light — light as a monkey.

sanskrit: taṃ samutsṛjya sā śaktiḥ saumitriṃ yudhi durjayam rāvaṇasya rathe tasmin sthānaṃ punar upāgamat
english: Having released Saumitri, that invincible one in battle, the śakti returned again to its place on Rāvaṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'pi mahātejāḥ prāpya saṃjñāṃ mahāhave ādade niśitān bāṇāñ jagrāha ca mahad dhanuḥ
english: Rāvaṇa of great blazing energy, having regained his senses in the great battle, took up sharp arrows and grasped his great bow.

sanskrit: āśvastaś ca viśalyaś ca lakṣmaṇaḥ śatrusūdanaḥ viṣṇor bhāgam amīmāṃsyam ātmānaṃ pratyanusmaran
english: And Lakṣmaṇa the slayer of enemies, comforted and freed from the arrow's pain, contemplated within himself his own nature as the unquestionable portion of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: nipātitamahāvīrāṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūm rāghavas tu raṇe dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaṃ samabhidravat
english: But Rāghava, seeing the great host of monkeys with their mighty heroes struck down in battle, charged toward Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: athainam upasaṃgamya hanūmān vākyam abravīt mama pṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya rakṣasaṃ śāstum arhasi
english: Then Hanūmān approached him and spoke: "Mount upon my back and punish that rākṣasa."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā rāghavo vākyaṃ vāyuputreṇa bhāṣitam ārohat sahasā śūro hanūmantaṃ mahākapim rathasthaṃ rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye dadarśa manujādhipaḥ
english: Hearing those words spoken by the son of Vāyu, the heroic Rāghava swiftly mounted great Hanūmān, and the lord of men beheld Rāvaṇa standing in his chariot on the battlefield.

sanskrit: tam ālokya mahātejāḥ pradudrāva sa rāghavaḥ vairocanam iva kruddho viṣṇur abhyudyatāyudhaḥ
english: Beholding him, Rāghava of great blazing energy charged forward, as Viṣṇu in fury charged at Vairocana with weapon upraised.

sanskrit: jyāśabdam akarot tīvraṃ vajraniṣpeṣanisvanam girā gambhīrayā rāmo rākṣasendram uvāca ha
english: Rāma made a fierce twang of his bowstring like the crash of a thunderbolt, and spoke to the lord of rākṣasas with a deep and resonant voice.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mama tvaṃ hi kṛtvā vipriyam īdṛśam kva nu rākṣasaśārdūla gato mokṣam avāpsyasi
english: "Stand! Stand! You have done me such grievous wrong — where, O tiger among rākṣasas, can you go to find escape?"

sanskrit: yadīndravaivasvata bhāskarān vā svayambhuvaiśvānaraśaṃkarān vā gamiṣyasi tvaṃ daśa vā diśo vā tathāpi me nādya gato vimokṣyase
english: "Even if you flee to Indra, Vaivasvata, or Bhāskara, to Svayambhū, Vaiśvānara, or Śaṃkara, or to the ten directions — even so, having gone from me today, you shall not be released."

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa śaktyābhihatas tvayādya icchan viṣādaṃ sahasābhyupetaḥ sa eṣa rakṣogaṇarāja mṛtyuḥ saputradārasya tavādya yuddhe
english: "And he whom you struck today with the śakti and who has suddenly fallen into affliction — he, O king of the rākṣasa host, is your death in today's battle, the death of you and your sons and wives."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā rākṣasendro mahākapim ājaghāna śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kālānalaśikhopamaiḥ
english: Hearing Rāghava's words, the lord of rākṣasas struck great Hanūmān with sharp arrows resembling the flames of the fire of final dissolution.

sanskrit: rākṣasenāhave tasya tāḍitasyāpi sāyakaiḥ svabhāvatejoyuktasya bhūyas tejo vyavardhata
english: Even as he was struck by those arrows in the rākṣasa battle, his energy — joined to his innate blazing power — only grew greater still.

sanskrit: tato rāmo mahātejā rāvaṇena kṛtavraṇam dṛṣṭvā plavagaśārdūlaṃ krodhasya vaśam eyivān
english: Then Rāma of great blazing energy, seeing that tiger among monkeys wounded by Rāvaṇa, came under the sway of wrath.

sanskrit: tasyābhisaṃkramya rathaṃ sacakraṃ sāśvadhvajacchatramahāpatākam sasārathiṃ sāśaniśūlakhaḍgaṃ rāmaḥ praciccheda śaraiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ
english: Advancing against his chariot, Rāma with well-feathered arrows cut apart its wheels, horses, flagstaff, parasol, great banner, charioteer, and thunderbolt, spear, and sword.

sanskrit: athendraśatruṃ tarasā jaghāna bāṇena vajrāśanisaṃnibhena bhujāntare vyūḍhasujātarūpe vajreṇa meruṃ bhagavān ivendraḥ
english: Then he swiftly struck the enemy of Indra with an arrow like a thunderbolt and lightning-flash in the broad well-formed expanse of his chest — as divine Indra strikes Meru with his thunderbolt.

sanskrit: yo vajrapātāśanisaṃnipātān na cukṣubhe nāpi cacāla rājā sa rāmabāṇābhihato bhṛśārtaś cacāla cāpaṃ ca mumoca vīraḥ
english: He who had never trembled or stirred at the fall of thunderbolt and lightning — that king, that hero, when struck by Rāma's arrow, reeled greatly in pain and dropped his bow.

sanskrit: taṃ vihvalantaṃ prasamīkṣya rāmaḥ samādade dīptam athārdhacandram tenārkavarṇaṃ sahasā kirīṭaṃ ciccheda rakṣo'dhipater mahātmāḥ
english: Seeing him reeling, great-souled Rāma took up a blazing crescent-headed arrow and with it suddenly cut away the crown of the lord of rākṣasas — brilliant as the sun.

sanskrit: taṃ nirviṣāśīviṣasaṃnikāśaṃ śāntārciṣaṃ sūryam ivāprakāśam gataśriyaṃ kṛttakirīṭakūṭam uvāca rāmo yudhi rākṣasendram
english: Seeing him like a venomous serpent whose venom is spent, like the sun with dimmed rays and extinguished glory, his crown-peak severed, Rāma spoke to the lord of rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ tvayā karma mahat subhīmaṃ hatapravīraś ca kṛtas tvayāham tasmāt pariśrānta iti vyavasya na tvaṃ śarair mṛtyuvaśaṃ nayāmi
english: "You have done a great and most terrible deed, and you have laid low my foremost heroes. Therefore, judging you to be exhausted, I shall not consign you to the power of death by my arrows today."

sanskrit: sa evam ukto hatadarpaharṣo nikṛttacāpaḥ sa hatāśvasūtaḥ śarārditaḥ kṛttamahākirīṭo viveśa laṅkāṃ sahasā sma rājā
english: Thus addressed, his pride and joy shattered, his bow severed, his horses and charioteer slain, tormented by arrows, his great crown cut away, the king swiftly retreated into Laṅkā.

sanskrit: tasmin praviṣṭe rajanīcarendre mahābale dānavadevaśatrau harīn viśalyān sahalakṣmaṇena cakāra rāmaḥ paramāhavāgre
english: As that lord of the night-rangers — mighty, the enemy of dānavas and gods — entered the city, Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, at the forefront of the supreme battle, made the monkeys free from wounds.

sanskrit: tasmin prabhagne tridaśendraśatrau surāsurā bhūtagaṇā diśaś ca sasāgarāḥ sarṣimahoragāś ca tathaiva bhūmyambucarāś ca hṛṣṭāḥ
english: As that enemy of the lord of the thirty gods was put to flight, the gods and asuras, the host of beings, the directions with their oceans, the great serpents together with the sages, and likewise the creatures of earth and water — all were filled with joy.
